method.title: Methodology — how to read these numbers

thas.body: Data come from the Taiwan Healthcare-associated infection and Antimicrobial resistance Surveillance system (THAS) antimicrobial-resistance module, as published in Taiwan CDC's annual reports (2022–2024 editions, data years 2017–2024).

sir.body: Each laboratory reports its own susceptible / intermediate / resistant interpretation. No single CLSI breakpoint edition is imposed, so breakpoint and method differences between hospitals carry into the national figures.

ns.body: Antibiogram values are 100 − %S, i.e. intermediate plus resistant. MDRO phenotypes (e.g. CRKP = carbapenem non-susceptible K. pneumoniae) follow the report's definitions.

suppress.body: Percentages based on fewer than 20 tested isolates, and agents not recommended by CLSI for the organism, are not printed and appear blank.

precision.body: Table values are exact; values quoted in report text are exact to the printed decimal; values read from printed charts are accurate to about ±1–2 percentage points and are drawn with hollow markers.

coho.body: Following THAS, isolates from outpatients, the emergency department or the first two days of admission are community-onset (CO); isolates collected from hospital day 3 onward are hospital-onset (HO).

dedup.body: When a data year appears in more than one edition, the more precise value is used, then the newest edition (historical counts are revised as reporting hospitals change).

firstIsolate.body: Antibiograms count the first isolate per patient, species and year in each hospital (worst result on the same day), limiting duplicate-isolate bias.

method.title: How antibiotic use is measured
method.ddd: Defined Daily Dose — the assumed average maintenance dose per day for a drug used for its main indication in adults, set by the WHO Collaborating Centre for Drug Statistics Methodology.
method.did: DDD per 1,000 patient-days — the standard hospital consumption density (inpatient). Population-level data instead use DDD per 1,000 inhabitants per day.
method.didFormula: DID = (total grams dispensed ÷ DDD in grams) ÷ patient-days × 1,000. DDDs make different drugs comparable, but do not reflect actual prescribed doses (e.g. paediatric or renal dosing).
method.aware: The WHO AWaRe antibiotic book groups antibiotics by their resistance potential to guide stewardship:
method.awareAccess: first- or second-choice drugs for common infections, lower resistance potential.
method.awareWatch: higher resistance potential; priority targets for stewardship.
method.awareReserve: last-resort options for confirmed or suspected multidrug-resistant infections.
method.target: The UN General Assembly (2024) and WHO's 13th General Programme of Work set a target that at least 70% of total antibiotic use should be Access antibiotics by 2030.
method.prov: The dataset is a provisional model with plausible magnitudes and trends, generated so that the views work before the official report is transcribed. It is flagged provisional in its data envelope and on every chart.

method.title: How HAIs are measured
method.tnis: The Taiwan Healthcare-associated infection Surveillance system (TNIS) collects ICU infection events from participating hospitals using definitions adapted from the US CDC NHSN.
method.density: HAI events per 1,000 patient-days in the ICU (all infection sites).
method.clabsi: Central line-associated bloodstream infections per 1,000 central-line days.
method.cauti: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections per 1,000 urinary-catheter days.
method.vap: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (or ventilator-associated events) per 1,000 ventilator days.
method.denom: Densities use patient-days; device-associated rates use device-days, so a unit with fewer devices can have a low CLABSI count but a high rate. Read rates together with utilisation ratios.
method.sir: The standardised infection ratio (observed ÷ predicted infections, risk-adjusted by unit type and hospital characteristics) is the preferred benchmark in NHSN. It is not shown here because the model data do not include predicted counts.
method.prov: The hai and hai_pathogens datasets are provisional models with plausible magnitudes and trends so that the views work before the official report is transcribed.

cors.d: GitHub Pages sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so any web page can call fetch() directly.

caching.d: Files change only when their content changes; GitHub Pages caches for about 10 minutes. Use generatedAt to detect a new build.

versioning.d: v1 paths are stable: fields may be added, but existing fields are never renamed or removed.

licence.d: Cite the original source listed in each envelope’s sources[] (the Taiwan CDC reports) and credit TW-AMR Watch as transcriber. Details under “Cite & licence” below.

embed.title: Embed builder
embed.lead: Choose a chart and its parameters and watch the live preview on the right. Copy the one-line <script> or the <iframe> into your hospital website, intranet portal or slides.
embed.scriptBody: The loader replaces itself with an auto-height iframe. This is the recommended option.
embed.iframeBody: Use this where scripts are not allowed. Set the height yourself, or resize automatically with the postMessage listener below.
embed.heightBody: Whenever its content height changes, the embed page posts { type: 'twamr:resize', id, height } to the parent page. embed.js handles this for you; with a plain iframe add the listener below.

intranet.d: Show national CRAB/CRKP/MRSA trends on the infection-control page for comparison with your own data.

committee.d: Embed with fixed level/years parameters so the figure follows the latest report before each meeting.

stewardship.d: Put the pathogen × antibiotic heatmap on training pages to inform empirical-therapy choices.

public.d: A hospital website or patient-education page can show headline indicators; keep the source line and provisional chips visible.

embed.provNote: Embedded cards behave like the site: provisional datasets carry a “Provisional” chip and chart-read values a precision badge. Please do not hide them.

cite.title: Cite & licence
cite.lead: When you use charts or data from this site, please cite both the dashboard and the original Taiwan CDC reports.
cite.dashboardText: TW-AMR Watch contributors. ({year}). TW-AMR Watch: Taiwan antimicrobial resistance surveillance dashboard [Data visualization]. {url} (accessed {date})
cite.cdcBody: When a figure comes from one of these editions, cite that edition:
cite.licenceData: The source reports are © Taiwan CDC (Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan). Values transcribed here remain subject to the original source’s terms of use; please credit the source when reusing them.
cite.licenceCode: The dashboard code is MIT-licensed (as stated in the README). The repository does not yet include a LICENSE file, so the exact licence text is to be confirmed.
cite.licenceProv: Provisional datasets (antibiotic use, HAI, international comparison) are model estimates; do not cite them as official data.

purpose.lead: TW-AMR Watch turns the Taiwan CDC’s published annual AMR surveillance reports into an interactive, downloadable and embeddable dashboard, so front-line staff can see trends without digging through PDFs.
purpose.body: It also offers an international comparison with WHO GLASS, layouts for antibiotic use and healthcare-associated infections, a static data API and a trilingual AMR assistant. Every value carries its source and precision so it can be read and cited correctly.

ic.d: National and hospital-level benchmarks for your own surveillance.

micro.d: Antibiograms and trends by organism and drug.

id.d: Evidence for empirical therapy and stewardship.

epi.d: JSON/CSV and API access for further analysis.

purpose.notice: This is an independent project, not an official publication of Taiwan CDC or WHO, and not medical advice. Check the original reports before citing any figure.

sources.lead: The resistance and isolate-count data are transcribed from three editions of the Taiwan CDC Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Annual Report (the AR module of the THAS surveillance system), covering data years 2017–2024. Use the SHA-256 values to confirm that your PDF is the same file.
sources.hospitalsNote: From {from} to {to}, as stated in the reports; the 2022 edition lists 210 in 2022.
sources.dataYearsNote: Each of the {n} reports covers about six years; overlapping years use the newest edition.
sources.verify: To verify, download the PDF and run sha256sum (or shasum -a 256), then compare with the hash above.

produced.lead: The reports are PDFs that mix text-layer tables with image charts, so three transcription methods were used and each value records its method (the precision field); the interface shows the matching badge.

table.d: Antibiograms (figures 3-1-x) and isolate-count tables (tables 2-x) are read straight from the PDF text layer and checked against the printed totals. Grey cells (n<20) are excluded.

text.d: Values stated in the report narrative or captions, e.g. “national CRAB rose from 55.1% in 2019 to 58.4% in 2024”, are recorded as printed.

chart.d: Bar and line charts (figures 3-2-x, 4-x-y) carry no value labels, so transcribers read the printed charts by eye and rounded to 0.5.

produced.dedupAria: Priority: table over text over chart estimate, then newest edition
produced.dedupBody: When a data point appears in several editions, the more exact value wins (table > text > chart estimate), and between equals the newest edition wins. Isolate-count tables are taken whole from the newest edition so rankings are never mixed. Reports revise history, so one trend line can mix points from different editions.
produced.mapping: Organism and drug names are mapped to stable codes using the report appendix; for MDRO charts (I+R) is the non-susceptible count and (S) the susceptible count, and neither is ever added to totals. The full rules are in docs/DATA.md.

nonsus.d: In antibiograms “% resistant” is 100 − %S, i.e. the non-susceptible share including intermediate (I); MDRO trends use the %R as printed in the report.

onset.d: Infections are split by the onset setting reported to THAS. Hospital-onset resistance is almost always higher than community-onset, so keep onset fixed when comparing.

levels.d: Medical centres (醫學中心), regional hospitals (區域醫院) and district hospitals (地區醫院), as accredited by the Ministry of Health and Welfare. “All” pools every reporting hospital; case mix differs by level, so do not rely on the national average alone.

suppress.d: The reports hide results when fewer than 20 isolates were tested or when CLSI does not recommend the drug for that organism (grey cells or *). This site does not fill them in, so a gap means “not shown”.

first.d: Per report notes: one result per hospital, patient, year, species and antibiotic, using the first specimen date; if that date has several results the worst is kept in the order NS > R > I > SDD > S.

precision.d: “Read from chart” values carry roughly ±1–2 points of error and should not be used to judge differences smaller than 2 points; a card shows the badge of its least exact value.

prov.lead: The Antibiotic Use and Healthcare-associated Infection annual reports have not been supplied yet, so the datasets below are provisional estimates modelled on published trends, not official data:
prov.why: These sections show a “Provisional” chip and a notice. In the international comparison the other countries’ values are approximate, while the Taiwan values are computed from the real resistance data. The labels disappear automatically once the official reports are ingested.
prov.howTitle: How to add the AMU / HAI report PDFs
prov.s1: Put the PDF in the repository’s raw/ folder; the file name must contain the Gregorian year and 「使用量」 or 「感染」, e.g. 臺灣抗生素使用量監視年報(2024年).pdf.
prov.s2: Push to GitHub; the ingest workflow regenerates public/data and public/api/v1 (locally run scripts/ingest/run_all.sh).
prov.s3: The mappers map_amu.py / map_hai.py are skeletons that must be adapted to the real table layout; once done, the dataset’s provisional flag becomes false.

credits.body: TW-AMR Watch is an independent project built on open data and open-source tools.
credits.data: Data: Taiwan CDC (Ministry of Health and Welfare), Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Annual Reports 2022–2024; the THAS surveillance system and the hospitals and laboratories that report to it.
credits.who: The international comparison draws on WHO GLASS and national surveillance reports; terminology follows WHO AWaRe, CLSI and EUCAST.
credits.oss: Open-source tools: React, Vite, Apache ECharts, Framer Motion, html-to-image, world-atlas and topojson-client.
credits.contactBody: Report data errors, transcription problems, broken links or feature ideas as a GitHub issue. For questions about the official statistics, contact Taiwan CDC.

access.lead: We aim for the spirit of WCAG 2.2 AA and keep improving:
access.kbd: Every control works with the keyboard, focus rings are visible, and a “skip to content” link is provided.
access.sr: Every chart has a text label (aria-label) and a toggleable data table, so screen-reader users get the same values.
access.contrast: Text contrast is at least 4.5:1, and colour is never the only carrier of meaning (labels and numbers accompany it).
access.motion: Motion is reduced automatically when your system asks for reduced motion.
access.lang: The interface is available in Traditional Chinese, English and Japanese, and the page language attribute follows your choice.
access.limits: Known limitations: hover details of the interactive map and some charts are available only through the data-table view. If you hit a barrier, please tell us.

privacy.lead: This is a static site with no back-end server and no accounts, and it does not track you.
privacy.none: No analytics, advertising or third-party cookies are used.
privacy.local: Only interface preferences (language, theme) are stored locally in your browser and never sent anywhere.
privacy.key: The optional Claude API key for the AMR assistant stays in your browser and is sent only directly to the Anthropic API, never through this site.
privacy.external: External links and social-share buttons lead to third-party sites, which have their own privacy policies.
privacy.host: The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which may keep ordinary server access logs under GitHub’s own policy.
